question: What does LPG cooking gas contain?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Propane and butane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) primarily consists of a mixture of **propane (C3H8) and butane (C4H10)**.
 
• These hydrocarbons are obtained during the refining of crude oil or extracted from natural gas streams.
 
• Propane and butane are stored in liquid form under moderate pressure, making them easily transportable and storable.
 
• When released from the storage container, they return to gaseous form for use in cooking, heating, and other applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy Content:**

 
 
• LPG has a high energy content, with a calorific value of approximately 46.1 MJ/kg for propane and 45.7 MJ/kg for butane.
 
• This makes it an efficient source of energy for heating and cooking purposes.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• LPG burns more cleanly than other fossil fuels, producing fewer pollutants like carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, and particulates.
 
• It is considered a greener alternative to traditional biomass fuels used in many households.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• LPG is highly flammable, and proper safety measures must be adhered to during storage and use.
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Besides cooking, LPG is used in heating, hot water systems, and as fuel for certain vehicles.
 
• It is also utilized in various industrial processes, such as metal cutting and drying operations.
